warranted_exact_choices: Both trails have equal total elevation gain, but Trail B has a gentler slope.
items.decisive_reasoning: Both100m gains are explicit; spread over1km versus2km they give average grades10% and5% if distances are horizontal. B is gentler on average. No claim about every local segment is warranted.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Trail A has greater elevation gain and a steeper slope.
choice_reasons.reason: Wrong: gains are explicitly equal, even though A has the greater mean grade.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Both trails have equal total elevation gain, but Trail A has a gentler slope.
choice_reasons.reason: Wrong: equal gain is correct but the mean-grade comparison is reversed.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Both trails have equal total elevation gain, but Trail B has a gentler slope.
choice_reasons.reason: Supported in the ordinary route-average comparison; it does not prove uniform slopes throughout.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Trail B has greater elevation gain and a gentler slope.
choice_reasons.reason: Wrong: B has no greater stated gain.

items.premise_concerns: Adequate for mean slope, not a full profile. Do not infer100m from five crossed lines; it is given.
items.distractor_reason: Two rivals contradict the explicitly equal gains; the reversed-slope choice is plausible, but three genuinely challenging distinct errors are not established.

difficulty.reason: One direct equal-rise/different-distance application. Contour count is unnecessary because gain is supplied; level2.

construction_uptake.extra_answer_claims: none: joint gain/slope comparison is legitimate

choice_reasons.exact_choice: the / The / the

items.premise_concerns: No unqualified answer meets all stated semantic requirements. This does not make the first completion ungrammatical.
items.distractor_reason: Only one option even begins with the requested ordinary a hotel; an hotel and A staff were are conspicuous distractor weaknesses.

warranted_exact_choices: Keep it in a well-draining rooting medium and wait for firm, creamy white roots and new growth before transplanting.
items.decisive_reasoning: Soft brown roots and no growth do not establish readiness; elapsed weeks alone are insufficient. A suitable rooting environment and healthy-root/growth indicators are the best-listed guide before moving to a longer-term pot.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Move it to soil immediately since three weeks is sufficient rooting time.
choice_reasons.reason: Wrong: three weeks does not guarantee healthy roots or readiness.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Keep it in a well-draining rooting medium and wait for firm, creamy white roots and new growth before transplanting.
choice_reasons.reason: Best-listed: corrects attention to suitable conditions and healthy-root/growth evidence. It is not a complete treatment plan or a guarantee that damaged roots recover.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Add rooting hormone to the water and transplant once roots appear longer.
choice_reasons.reason: Not warranted: hormone and greater length do not establish root health or readiness.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Switch to a larger water container to give roots more room to develop.
choice_reasons.reason: Not warranted: crowding is not established; larger water volume alone does not address the observed unhealthy roots.

items.premise_concerns: Accept as comparative advice, not diagnosis of a unique cause or an exhaustive damaged-root recovery protocol. Source does not promise that waiting alone repairs rot.
items.distractor_reason: Distinct timing-only, hormone/length-only and container-space diagnoses are plausible beginner errors; the last is weaker but relevant rather than absurd.

difficulty.reason: Directly applies the healthy-root readiness rule and rejects calendar time as sufficient. No independent interacting constraint makes it more than2.

construction_uptake.answer_dimensions: all choices propose next actions, though lengths and timing detail differ
construction_uptake.extra_answer_claims: three weeks sufficient is part of a wrong decision rationale; not an unrelated extra answer axis
construction_uptake.note: Descriptive construction evidence, not treatment identity or correctness credit.

warranted_exact_choices: The ridge trail is steeper; the valley trail is gentler, regardless of which is higher in elevation.
items.decisive_reasoning: At1:50000,5mm and10mm correspond to250m and500m. The same20m interval gives mean cross-contour grades8% and4%. The ridge is steeper; absolute elevations remain unknown.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: The ridge trail is steeper; the valley trail is gentler, regardless of which is higher in elevation.
choice_reasons.reason: Supported: smaller spacing at the same interval/scale means greater gradient, independent of absolute altitude.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: The valley trail is higher in elevation because wider spacing indicates higher ground.
choice_reasons.reason: Wrong: horizontal contour spacing indicates gradient, not absolute elevation.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: The ridge trail must be above 1000 meters due to the close contour spacing.
choice_reasons.reason: Wrong: no1000m label or elevation datum is supplied.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Both trails have identical slope steepness because they share the same contour interval.
choice_reasons.reason: Wrong: identical vertical interval does not make differing horizontal spacing equal in gradient.

items.premise_concerns: No local uniformity or safety inference. The same-map interval and scale are explicit.
items.distractor_reason: Altitude-versus-gradient and equal-interval confusions are plausible; the arbitrary1000m assertion is weak.

difficulty.reason: Closer contours indicate steeper terrain is the single decisive rule; scale arithmetic is optional. The frozen criteria classify this as1–2; rate2.

construction_uptake.answer_dimensions: mixed: correct slope comparison versus absolute-height claims and equal-slope claim
construction_uptake.extra_answer_claims: absolute1000m is an ungrounded dimension; the correct option's altitude-independence clause is relevant to the learning comparison
construction_uptake.note: Descriptive construction evidence, not treatment identity or correctness credit.

warranted_exact_choices: The pothos will root; the Monstera leaf will not develop into a new plant
items.decisive_reasoning: The pothos has usable stem nodes; a Monstera leaf/petiole without stem tissue cannot form a new plant. Will root is read as the requested ordinary reasonable expectation, not a universal guarantee.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Both will root successfully in water or solid media
choice_reasons.reason: Not a warranted successful-propagation prediction for both: roots alone would not establish a new Monstera plant. Do not claim detached leaves can never form roots.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: The pothos will root; the Monstera leaf will not develop into a new plant
choice_reasons.reason: Best complete outcome: viable pothos stem versus node-free Monstera inability to become a new plant. Ordinary reasonable-prediction scope matters for will.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: The Monstera leaf will root if given rooting hormone; the pothos will not
choice_reasons.reason: Wrong compound claim: no supplied basis for pothos not rooting; hormone cannot supply a missing Monstera growth node.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Neither will propagate without additional stem tissue from another plant
choice_reasons.reason: Wrong: the pothos already contains usable stem nodes and does not require donor tissue from another plant.

items.premise_concerns: Treat will as an ordinary expectation under the task wording; no unconditional success or proven impossibility of Monstera leaf root formation is asserted.
items.distractor_reason: Rivals largely repeat tissue/hormone confusion; the no-rooting pothos and extra-donor-tissue claims are weak. Root-only language is not interchangeable with new-plant growth.

difficulty.reason: One familiar species/tissue requirement eliminates rivals. Level2.

construction_uptake.answer_dimensions: mostly both plants, but root-only outcomes mix with new-plant outcomes
construction_uptake.extra_answer_claims: root-versus-new-plant shift is a material mismatch in outcome dimensions
construction_uptake.note: Descriptive construction evidence, not treatment identity or correctness credit.

warranted_exact_choices: Move Cutting A to a pot; keep Cutting B in its rooting medium
items.decisive_reasoning: A has healthy roots and active growth, supporting transfer. B has viable-node material but lacks healthy-root/growth readiness; deferring potting is preferable to immediate transfer or automatic disposal.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Move Cutting A to a pot; keep Cutting B in its rooting medium
choice_reasons.reason: Best-listed: distinguish readiness from retained propagation potential. Keeping B in rooting medium does not imply leaving harmful conditions unchanged.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Move both cuttings to pots immediately
choice_reasons.reason: Wrong: B has no demonstrated readiness for a longer-term pot.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Keep both cuttings in rooting medium until roots turn brown
choice_reasons.reason: Wrong: roots need not turn brown; unhealthy brown softness is a concern.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Discard Cutting B and apply rooting hormone to Cutting A
choice_reasons.reason: Not warranted: no evidence requires disposal of all B's viable tissue; hormone is not required for ready A.

items.premise_concerns: Best practical comparison, not a complete treatment plan or proof that passive waiting is sufficient. Source support for the exact recovery method remains limited.
items.distractor_reason: Pot-both and discard-B/hormone-A are plausible mismatches, but waiting specifically for brown roots is a conspicuous weak alternative.

difficulty.reason: Requires using contrasting root/growth observations while recognizing that B still has growth nodes;3 is plausible. It is a2/3-sensitive direct comparison, not evidence of multiple complex steps.

construction_uptake.answer_dimensions: mostly A/B management, though the last introduces hormone as a different action
construction_uptake.extra_answer_claims: no unrelated factual explanation clause; all are proposed management actions
construction_uptake.note: Descriptive construction evidence, not treatment identity or correctness credit.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: The pothos stem can root and grow; the Monstera leaf alone cannot develop into a new plant.

choice_reasons.reason: Wrong: pothos stem propagation is supported; layering is not required. Possible Monstera root formation alone does not validate the compound option.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Both nouns refer back to specific items established in the previous sentence.

choice_reasons.reason: Wrong gradient trend: spacing decreases, so slope magnitude increases rather than becoming gentler.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Elevation decreases and the slope becomes progressively steeper.
choice_reasons.reason: Conditional on descending elevations; direction is not supplied.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Elevation increases and the slope becomes progressively steeper.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: Elevation stays constant while the slope varies.
choice_reasons.reason: Not supported: crossing contours at different elevations is not a constant-elevation route.

items.premise_concerns: A sign-reversed elevation profile preserves every supplied spacing while reversing elevation direction. Do not infer uphill from increasing density.
items.distractor_reason: Two directional alternatives remain unresolved; a complete key is absent, so three refuted distractors cannot be established.

conditional_best_exact_choices: The second "a" is an error; it should be "the dough" for consistency.
items.decisive_reasoning: The mixture is recoverable from combining ingredients. On the ordinary continuous-recipe reading, the next action concerns the already formed dough, so the dough is the coherent choice. But a dough is grammatically possible for an arbitrary/new dough; the stem does not explicitly exclude that change of reference.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: "The mixture" refers to a specific result already created; "a dough" presents a new conceptual state.
choice_reasons.reason: Not warranted for the second a: dough was already introduced as dough; its repetition does not itself introduce a new conceptual state.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: "Dough" is countable, so it must use "a" while "mixture" is uncountable.
choice_reasons.reason: Wrong: both countability labels/necessity claims are overbroad; a mixture is grammatical and dough can take the.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: The second "a" is an error; it should be "the dough" for consistency.
choice_reasons.reason: Natural best correction for continuity of the same recipe batch, but error must mean reference/coherence mismatch, not universal ungrammaticality.

choice_reasons.exact_choice: "The" indicates a process step, while "a" indicates the final product.
choice_reasons.reason: Wrong: these articles do not encode process-step versus final-product categories.

items.premise_concerns: No unqualified proof of grammatical error. Conditional best is choice3 under the ordinary intended same-dough continuity; preserve possible alternate discourse readings.
items.distractor_reason: The conceptual-state rival is plausible, but the remaining invented countability/process rules are weak. The intended correction needs an explicit same-batch scope.

difficulty.reason: Direct reference continuity and a first/second mention correction, level2. Awkward wording and an implicit error diagnosis do not establish3.
